title: M/S Nageshwar Papers Limited v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited and Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Krishna Murari and Shailendra Kumar Agrawal, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed of by consent applying settled law: the respondents were directed to supply the petitioner a list of test laboratories approved by the National Accreditation Board of Testing and Calibration Laboratory under Clause 5.4(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the meter to be opened and tested only after the petitioner's choice from that list; and the respondents restrained from dismantling and testing the meter in their private lab.
headnote: On a writ by M/S Nageshwar Papers Ltd. seeking to restrain the licensee (Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.) from dismantling, breaking open or testing its meter in the licensee's private laboratory, and to compel supply of the list of approved test laboratories under Clause 5.4(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, a Division Bench held the issue settled by its earlier decisions in Smt. Amrawati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. (2009 (2) AWC 1189) and Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. (30.05.2014). Adopting Amrawati Devi, the Court reiterated that under Clause 5.6(c)(iii) a sealed defective meter is to be tested at the licensee's lab, an independent lab or by the Electrical Inspector as agreed by the consumer; that the consumer has a right to independent testing and the licensee a corresponding duty to apprise him of it, failing which the sealing proceedings are irregular and illegal; that a consumer is not deemed to have waived the right without knowledge of it (waiver requiring an intentional act with knowledge, per Moti Lal Padampat Sugar Mills); and that, after sealing, the licensee must serve a notice (printed in bold capital letters) for the consumer to exercise the testing option, whereafter a date is fixed for testing in his presence and the chosen agency's finding is final and binding. Applying this, the Court directed the respondents to supply the list of NABL-approved test laboratories under Clause 5.4(a), to open and test the meter only at the petitioner's chosen laboratory, and not to dismantle and test the meter in their private lab; the writ was disposed of accordingly.
facts: M/S Nageshwar Papers Limited, a consumer, filed WRIT-C No. 26590 of 2017 against Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited and another. With the consent of the parties, the Division Bench disposed of the petition without calling for a counter affidavit. The sole relief sought was a mandamus restraining the respondents from dismantling, breaking open or testing the petitioner's meter in their private laboratory, together with a mandamus to supply the list of approved test laboratories as provided in Clause 5.4(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 so that the meter could be tested after the petitioner exercised its choice from among the approved labs. The Court noted that the issue stood settled by the Division Bench decisions in Smt. Amrawati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. (2009 (2) AWC 1189) and Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. (Civil Misc. Writ Petition No. 55384 of 2009, decided 30.05.2014), and reproduced the relevant passages of Amrawati Devi (paragraphs 6 to 11) before issuing its directions.

reusable_constructions.construction: Under Clause 5.6(c)(iii) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 a sealed defective meter is to be tested at the licensee's laboratory, an independent laboratory or by the Electrical Inspector as agreed by the consumer; the consumer has a right to independent testing and the licensee a corresponding duty to apprise him of that right, and failure to discharge that duty renders the sealing proceedings irregular and illegal.

After sealing a defective meter, the licensee must serve on the consumer a notice, printed in bold capital letters, to exercise his option to have the meter tested by the Electrical Inspector, at the licensee's laboratory, or by one of the approved outside agencies named in the notice; once the option is exercised a date is fixed for testing in the consumer's presence, and the decision based on the option and the test report is final and binding on both licensee and consumer.

Under Clause 5.4(a) the licensee must supply the consumer the list of approved test laboratories (accredited by the National Accreditation Board of Testing and Calibration Laboratories) and test the meter only at the consumer's chosen approved laboratory; the meter cannot be dismantled and tested in the licensee's own private laboratory.

A consumer is not to be treated as having waived the right to independent meter-testing merely by not objecting, unless he had knowledge of the right; waiver requires an intentional act with full knowledge of the right, and there is no presumption that everyone knows the law (Moti Lal Padampat Sugar Mills).

holding_units.clause: 5.4(a) r/w 5.6(c)(iii) - supply of the list of approved test laboratories; testing at the consumer's chosen lab, not the licensee's private lab
holding_units.topic: Consumer's right to have a sealed meter tested at a chosen approved (NABL) laboratory; no private-lab testing
holding_units.question: Before testing a sealed defective meter, must the licensee supply the consumer the list of approved test laboratories under Clause 5.4(a) and test the meter only at the consumer's chosen approved lab, rather than in the licensee's own private laboratory?
holding_units.holding: Yes. Applying the settled law, the Court directed that the respondents provide the petitioner a list of test laboratories approved by the National Accreditation Board of Testing and Calibration Laboratory as provided in Clause 5.4(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, that the meter be opened and tested only after the petitioner's choice is made from that list, and that the respondents shall not dismantle the meter and test it in their private lab.

evidence.quote: it is directed that the respondents shall provide a list of test lab approved by National Accredition Board of Testing and Calibration Laboratory as provided in Clause 5.4(a) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and the meter shall be opened and tested only after the choice is given by the petitioner out of the list supplied to him.
It is further directed that the respondent shall not dismantle the meter and test the same in their private lab.

holding_units.flag: Proper judgment with printed page numbers (pp. 1-3); pins reference the printed pages. Paragraph numbers 6-11 appearing in the text belong to the reproduced Amrawati Devi judgment, not to this order.

holding_units.clause: 5.6(c)(iii) - defective meter tested as agreed by the consumer; right to independent testing and corresponding duty to apprise
holding_units.topic: Consumer's right to independent testing of a sealed defective meter and the licensee's duty to inform him of it
holding_units.question: Does a consumer have a right to have a sealed defective meter tested by an independent agency of his choice, and must the licensee apprise the consumer of that right before testing?
holding_units.holding: Yes. Adopting the Division Bench in Amrawati Devi as settled law, the Court held that under Clause 5.6(c)(iii) a defective meter, after sealing in the consumer's presence, is to be tested at the licensee's lab, an independent lab or by the Electrical Inspector as agreed by the consumer; the consumer has a right to get the meter tested by an independent agency, and the authorities have a corresponding duty to apprise the consumer of that right, failure of which renders the entire sealing proceedings irregular and illegal.

evidence.quote: The consumer has a right to get the meter tested with independent agency. The authorities, therefore, have a corresponding duty to apprise the consumer of the right.
renders the entire proceedings for sealing the meter irregular and illegal.

principle_tags.application: Following Amrawati Devi, the licensee must apprise the consumer of, and offer, the option of testing venue (Electrical Inspector / licensee's lab / an approved outside agency) before testing a sealed defective meter; failure to do so renders the sealing proceedings irregular and illegal.

lead_authorities.name: Smt. Amrawati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

principle_tags.application: A consumer cannot be held to have waived the right to independent meter-testing without knowledge of the Clause 5.6(c)(iii) right; waiver requires an intentional act with full knowledge, there being no presumption that everyone knows the law.

lead_authorities.name: M/s Moti Lal Padampat Sugar Mills Ltd. v. State of U.P.

principle_tags.application: The Court directed that the meter be tested only at a lab chosen by the consumer from the Clause 5.4(a) list of NABL-approved laboratories, and restrained the licensee from dismantling and testing the meter in its own private lab.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioner's meter was in fact defective, and any consequential assessment
not_decided.note: The Court directed only the procedure for testing (choice of an approved lab and no private-lab testing); it did not adjudicate the meter's actual condition or any assessment, which would follow the test result.

Mohd. Sagir (2014) - the other Division Bench decision (against the same DVVNL) on which the Court held the meter-testing issue to be settled.

authorities.proposition: Under Clause 5.6(c)(iii) a sealed defective meter is tested as agreed by the consumer; the consumer has a right to independent testing and the licensee a corresponding duty to apprise him, failing which the sealing proceedings are irregular and illegal; after sealing, a notice (in bold capitals) must be served for the consumer to exercise the testing option, and the resulting test report is final and binding.
authorities.how_treated: Extensively reproduced (paragraphs 6-11) and followed as the settled law governing the relief granted.

authorities.how_treated: Cited alongside Amrawati Devi as settling the issue; followed.

authorities.name: M/s Moti Lal Padampat Sugar Mills Ltd. v. State of U.P. and others
authorities.proposition: Waiver means the abandonment of a right; it must be an intentional act with full knowledge of the right, and there is no presumption that everyone knows the law.
